clue.text: Pack a US resort

parts.note: to pack down earth or tobacco is to tamp it

explanation.surface: Someone is told to get their bags ready for a trip to an American holiday spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pack' looks like an instruction about luggage, but here it means press down firmly.
explanation.definitionFit: Tampa is a Florida city on the Gulf coast, popular with holidaymakers.

clue.text: Easily created, and quickly disposed of

explanation.surface: Something made with little effort and dumped just as fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Work dashed off is produced casually; a garment flung aside is discarded hastily.

clue.text: Doesn't take exams seriously?

parts.note: reads as a careless student but means makes fun of, while also naming practice exams sat before the real ones

explanation.surface: A student who treats tests lightly.
explanation.walkthrough: Mock exams are trial papers sat by British school pupils before the real ones.
explanation.definitionFit: To ridicule is not to take something seriously, and practice exams carry the same name.

clue.text: A mariner initially speaks in favour of a big old vessel

indicators.note: only the first letter of mariner is wanted
the phrase for supporting something with a is spoken, so only its sound counts

parts.note: in favour of is for, followed by a

explanation.surface: A sailor begins by speaking up for a large ancient ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'speaks' turns FOR A into its sound-alike PHORA.
explanation.definitionFit: An amphora is a large two-handled jar used in ancient Greece and Rome.

clue.text: Struggle to get rid of termagant

parts.note: a struggle or fight is a battle
to axe something is to cut it or get rid of it

explanation.surface: Someone is fighting hard to be rid of a shrewish woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A termagant is a harsh, overbearing woman, the same figure as the domineering harridan of the idiom.

clue.text: I go red all round, rather like the sky

indicators.note: the word for going red goes all round the letter I

parts.note: to blush is to go red

explanation.surface: Someone flushes red all over, though they look somewhat like the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: A clear sky is blue, and the suffix makes it 'somewhat blue'.

clue.text: Mrs Crummles, say, gyrating neat hips

indicators.note: the words neat hips spin round into a new order

explanation.surface: A theatrical lady swivels her trim hips.
explanation.walkthrough: Mrs Crummles is the actress wife of a theatre manager in Dickens's Nicholas Nickleby.
explanation.definitionFit: Mrs Crummles is an actress, an example of a stage performer.

clue.text: Youngster potentially ending up in jug?

definitions.text: Youngster potentially ending up in jug?

parts.words: Youngster potentially ending up in jug?
parts.note: a young animal destined, perhaps, for a stewing pot rather than a prison

explanation.surface: A young person who may land in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: Jugged hare is hare stewed in a jug; 'jug' is also slang for prison.
explanation.definitionFit: A young hare is the youngster, and hare is the classic animal cooked in a jug.

clue.text: Honour satisfied at last in a formal speech

indicators.note: the final letter is placed inside the run of a and the speech

parts.note: an oration is a formal speech

indicators.note: only the last letter of satisfied is wanted

explanation.surface: Being contented at last with an honour bestowed in a formal address.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoration is worship or deep reverence, a way of honouring someone.

clue.text: Lifted a veil to reveal Miss

annotationWithheld.why: Lifted a veil to reveal Miss (5): EVADE is EDAVE in 'liftED A VEil' read upwards, so 'Lifted' is both part of the hidden text and the reversal indicator.
annotationWithheld.clue: Lifted a veil to reveal Miss

clue.text: Completion of Exchange puts City into ecstasy

indicators.note: the City's letters are put into the word for ecstasy, splitting it after its first letter

parts.note: ecstasy is rapture
EC is the postcode of the City of London

explanation.surface: Finishing a deal on the Stock Exchange sends the City into raptures.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a financial exchange, but in chess an exchange is a trade of pieces, completed when the second piece is taken back.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess, the move that takes back a piece after your own was captured completes the trade of material.

clue.text: Sebastian's sister receives a bow

explanation.surface: A brother's sibling takes a bow on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: Sebastian and his twin sister are characters in Shakespeare's Twelfth Night; the second reading is the stringed instrument, played with a bow.
explanation.definitionFit: Viola is Sebastian's twin in Twelfth Night; the instrument of that name is played by drawing a bow across it.

clue.text: Where to see a marvellous animal on film, some say

indicators.note: in an across clue, the marvellous animal comes on, that is after, the film
the word for a type of film is pronounced loosely, as some speakers would say it

parts.note: a western is a cowboy film
super means marvellous
a mare is a female horse

explanation.surface: Asking where to watch a wonderful creature in a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: WESTON-SUPER-MARE is a seaside resort in Somerset, England. Said quickly, its first part sounds like 'western', the cowboy film.
explanation.definitionFit: A place name answers the question of where, and this town is the place to see the 'super mare'.

clue.text: Stress test: lead breaks, gold comes first

indicators.note: the gold is placed before the rest of the letters

parts.note: OR is the heraldic word for gold

indicators.note: the word lead is broken up and its letters reformed

explanation.surface: A test of strength: a lead pipe snaps and gold takes priority.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordeal is a severe trial, a painful experience that tests endurance.

clue.text: The main hazard is snow heaped on trees

indicators.note: in a down clue the snow sits on top of the trees

parts.note: snow heaped by wind is a drift
a wood is a group of trees

explanation.surface: A danger: snow piled up on the trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is the sea, not 'the chief'.
explanation.definitionFit: Floating timber is a danger to ships at sea.

clue.text: Kitchen equipment goes into food stores

parts.note: a pan is a piece of kitchen equipment
someone who has goes at something tries it

explanation.surface: Cooking gear is moved into the larder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' simply joins the pieces; 'goes' means attempts, as in having a go.
explanation.definitionFit: Pantries are small rooms where provisions are kept.

clue.text: Dive from the height into waters unknown

indicators.note: the height is placed into the word for waters

parts.note: the seas are waters
a peak is a height
Y is an unknown quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: Diving from a great height into uncharted waters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dive' looks like a verb but is a seedy bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A dive is a disreputable drinking place, like an illicit Prohibition-era bar.

clue.text: Not hostile, even when cold inside

annotationWithheld.why: Not hostile, even when cold inside (8): AMICABLE is AMIABLE with C inside, but AMIABLE has no clue word except the definition 'Not hostile', which would do two jobs.
annotationWithheld.clue: Not hostile, even when cold inside

clue.text: Hoopla, for example, makes a' proper pursuit

explanation.surface: A fairground stall game is said to be a worthy hobby.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoopla is a game played at a funfair; a legitimate target for criticism or attack is a proper quarry.

clue.text: Hell raised, for example, over hair dye

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over the second
in a down clue the abbreviation is lifted, read upwards

parts.note: henna is a reddish hair dye

explanation.surface: All hell breaks loose over someone's hair colouring.
explanation.definitionFit: Gehenna is a biblical name for a place of torment, the underworld of the damned.

clue.text: Be dishonoured, but show resilience

explanation.surface: Someone is disgraced but springs back.
explanation.walkthrough: A cheque that is dishonoured by the bank is returned unpaid.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheque refused by the bank is returned; a ball that rebounds shows springiness.

clue.text: Fungal infection causing Hardy's Gabriel irritation

parts.note: Gabriel Oak is the shepherd hero of Thomas Hardy's Far from the Madding Crowd
gall is irritation or bitterness

explanation.surface: A fungal disease causing annoyance to a Hardy character.
explanation.definitionFit: A swelling on tree bark caused by a parasite, treated here as a growth on the tree.

clue.text: Oresteia could become tense, when ease 'of speech lost

indicators.note: Oresteia's letters may be reworked into something else once others go
the word ease is taken by its sound, which is two letter Es

parts.note: the word as written, said aloud

explanation.surface: A Greek tragedy might turn tense once it loses its fluency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' is part of the subtraction signal: the two Es, whose names together sound like 'ease', leave the play's title before what remains is reordered.
explanation.definitionFit: The aorist is a Greek verb tense expressing a simple past action.

clue.text: Relive the past, as one does in the autumn

definitions.text: as one does in the autumn

explanation.surface: Living in the past, as everyone does when autumn comes.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the clocks go back an hour at the end of summer time in October.
explanation.definitionFit: To return to old ways is to turn back time; in autumn people literally move their timepieces an hour earlier.

clue.text: Mongrel's constant grip

parts.note: pi is the mathematical constant
a dog is a gripping device or clamp

explanation.surface: A mutt's steady hold.
explanation.definitionFit: A pi-dog is a stray, ownerless dog of Asian villages, a cur of mixed breed.

clue.text: Cancel regular publication in absence of second article

indicators.note: the second of the two letter As in the word is left out

parts.note: an annual is a book published every year
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A regular periodical is axed because a second piece is missing.
explanation.definitionFit: To annul is to declare void, revoking something such as a marriage.

clue.text: Conversation about new murder, perhaps

indicators.note: the word for a chat is turned round

parts.note: a conversation is a word, as in having a word with someone

explanation.surface: Talk turns to a fresh killing.
explanation.definitionFit: Killing someone by holding them under water is one way to commit murder, so 'perhaps' marks an example.

clue.text: She's seen sitting on half a pound of metal

definitions.text: She's seen sitting on half a pound of metal

parts.words: She's seen sitting on half a pound of metal
parts.note: the seated female figure that appears on the British fifty-pence coin, and also a pewter-like alloy

explanation.surface: A woman perches on a chunk of metal weighing eight ounces.
explanation.walkthrough: The seated figure of Britannia appears on the 50p coin (half a pound sterling); Britannia metal is also a tin alloy.
explanation.definitionFit: The national personification of Britain sits on the fifty-pence piece, and the name also belongs to a tin alloy.

clue.text: On your behalf, he'll vow to get pardon for cracking up

indicators.note: the words get pardon fall apart and are rebuilt

explanation.surface: Someone promises on your behalf to win a reprieve for breaking down.
explanation.definitionFit: At a christening, a sponsor makes the baptismal promises on behalf of the infant.

clue.text: French composer's cradle-song with a couple of notes missing

definitions.note: the 's reads as 'is', so the definition is the composer himself

indicators.note: the named notes are left out of the word for a cradle-song

parts.note: a cradle-song is a lullaby sung to a baby
A and B are two musical notes

explanation.surface: A French composer's lullaby with two notes absent.
explanation.walkthrough: Jean-Baptiste Lully was the court composer of Louis XIV.
explanation.definitionFit: Lully was a seventeenth-century composer at the court of Versailles.
